Update fields of a Zotero item

Source: R/item.R
cz_update_item.Rd

Changes selected fields of one item and shows exactly what will change. The default is a dry run: the item is read and a before/after diff is shown, but nothing is written. Use dry_run = FALSE to write.

Usage

cz_update_item(
  item,
  fields,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  auth = cz_auth(),
  cache = getOption("citezot.cache", FALSE)
)

Arguments

item

The item: a DOI, Zotero item ID, citekey, or one-row result of cz_find().

fields

A named list of new values, e.g. list(date = "in press", DOI = "10.1234/abc"). Names must be fields that exist for the item's type; see names(cz_get_item(item)$data).

dry_run

If TRUE (default), show the diff and write nothing.

auth

Credentials from cz_auth() (a key with write access to write).

cache

Passed to cz_fetch_items() when item has to be looked up.

Value

Invisibly, a list with item, changes (for each changed field, its before and after) and written.

Details

Only fields whose value actually changes are sent (a PATCH), together with If-Unmodified-Since-Version: if the item was edited elsewhere since it was read, Zotero rejects the write (HTTP 412) and nothing is overwritten.

Plain fields take a single string (use "" to clear one). creators, tags, collections and relations take lists and are replaced as a whole, so to add one tag pass the full list of tags. Identity and bookkeeping fields (key, version, itemType, dates, parentItem, deleted) can't be changed, and the citekey is changed with cz_pin_key().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"))                  # preview
cz_update_item("Regnier2024", list(date = "in press"), dry_run = FALSE) # write
} # }
